anika: FYI bringing Argos-7B (llama-fork) up in int8. Conversion + quant looked fine but evals show weird long-context hallucinations after 8k tokens. anyone seen tokenizer-normalization gotchas with these family models?

samir: how big is the regression? any diffs with fp16 baseline? could be rotary scale or kv-cache token id shift.

anika: fp16 baseline on our long-doc QA set: EM 78.4%. int8 post-convert: EM 61.2%. short prompts fine, drop only manifests after ~3k tokens. sample: prompt asks to continue list, model invents new sections not present.

anika: conversion log snippet:```
python convert.py --from=argos --to=rwk --norm=NFC --quant=bitsandbytes
# tokenizer.used_normalizer = "compat_legacy"
# vocab size 50288
```

jeff: that normalizer flag rings a bell. Argos tokeniser preserves some combined glyphs (no NFKC). We had a similar drift when mixing vocab.normalized vs normalized_unicoded in another bring-up. missing decomp can change token offsets for long prefixes and break cache alignment.

marta: also check rotary angle scaling. Argos uses head_dim=128 while our default reference was 96 in the conversion/runtime mapping. If you don't rescale rotary frequencies, the sin/cos lookup alignment shifts with head-dim and long-context attention accumulates phase error => slow drift.

anika: good catch. I pulled kv-cache traces and saw steady attenuation in attention mass for early tokens (they become "less attended") which aligns with phase mismatch hypothesis.

samir: we should run two quick experiments: 1) force tokenizer NFKC on input before encoding, 2) rescale rotary angles by sqrt(head_ref/head_target) or linear interp of frequency table and compare.

anika: ran both. Results: forcing NFKC recovered ~8% EM (to 69.5%). Rescaling rotary using head_ratio = target/ref gave additional lift to 74.8%. Combined -> 76.9% (nearly back to fp16). Numbers from eval-batch 4512 (long-doc QA).

anika: snippet of rotation rescale implemented in the serving shim:```
# pseudo
def rescale_rotary_angles(angles, head_ref, head_target):
    scale = (head_ref / head_target) ** 0.5
    return angles * scale
```

marta: sqrt head_ratio is what we tried before and it empirically matches phase density. Another lightweight option: build a tiny adapter on KV proj: per-head learnable scale (initialized from sqrt ratio) and bake into conversion so runtime uses same matrix in int8 path. that avoids tinkering with kernel internals.

jeff: also for tokenizer, we added a small conversion step in the converter:```
# conversion hook
with open(vocab) as f: tokens = normalize_unicode(f.read(), form='NFKC')
write_new_vocab(tokens)
```
so onboarding pipeline always emits normalized vocab + mapping table.

anika: implemented the per-head adapter (4k params) and included it in the quant path (baked into QK, re-quantized). ran full int8 eval: EM 77.1% (vs fp16 78.4). latency +2.5% P95. quality regressions mostly closed.

ci-bot: ml-eval pipeline completed: run-4512 -> status: finished, artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/4512/ (diff report attached) :white_check_mark:

samir: nice. next steps: 1) add tokenizer normalization step to converter; 2) add head-dim rotary rescale unit test (small dynamic test coverage); 3) add a quant-smoke test that runs long-context QA for >=4k tokens in CI; 4) open PR linking evaluation artifacts.

anika: will open PR with: conv + adapter + unit tests + eval artifacts. pinging @samir @jeff for review once draft is up. thanks all. :pray:

eval-bot: note: created issue #ML-1209 for "Argos int8 long-context drift - tokenizer + rotary adapter" with links to run-4512.

jeff: leaving a reminder: check vocab aliasing for punctuation clusters (",--" vs "—"), those caused a micro-token-shift in one earlier conversion.

anika: noted, adding a small fuzz test for punctuation clusters. will post PR link in this thread when ready.
